\[
I_{\text{out}}(x,y,c) = I(x,y,c)\,\bigl(1 + \sigma\, n(x,y,c)\bigr),
\qquad
n \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\,1)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(n\): A standard normal random number
- \(\sigma\): The standard deviation of the factor

Each value is multiplied by a random factor with mean 1 and standard deviation sigma. This is the "speckle" mode of skimage.util.random_noise, written with a standard deviation instead of a variance. Black stays black, and the noise grows with the brightness. The normal numbers come from the same position-based generator as Add Gaussian noise.
